Books FAQ

When are new books dropped?

We drop 5-7 new books on the first of the month at 8am ET. Yes, even January 1st! We drop the 1st rain or shine, holiday or not!

Do I get to pick my books?

Yes! Every month members can select 1 book using their credit and purchase up to 2 extra books at a discount. The first book must be from the newest month’s picks but the extra books can be from any month.

What types of books do you carry?

We carry a range of genres from horror to literary fiction to romance to thriller and more! We love spotlighting debut voices and introducing our members to under-the-radar picks. We have a full-time editorial team dedicated to curating our selections.

Do you offer e-books or audiobooks?

We exclusively offer hardcover Aardvark editions with a matte dust jacket and buttery soft hardcover underneath. Check under the dust jacket and you’ll notice a foiled hardcover spine. Hardcover > ebooks any day. Our books won’t die on a trans-Atlantic flight!

Can I order a box without a book from the current month?

No, every order must include at least one book from the current month’s selections. Your add-ons (up to 2) can be from any month.

How do I remove a book from my box in-app?

You can remove a book from your box by following these steps:

1. Click the book that is on your box and view its page with the synopsis

2. Click the "View in box" button in the bottom

3. Click the top right corner of a book that you'd like to remove

Will out-of-stock books come back?

Very rarely, our team is focused on carrying upcoming picks for our members!

Do I get to keep my books?

Yes, they’re yours to read, donate, share, annotate or hoard! Loan them to friends at your own risk!

Membership

How much does membership cost, my wallet is asking?

In the USA, membership is $17.99 USD/month (accounts for 1 book) and $10.99 for each extra book. In Canada, membership is $25.99 CAD/month (accounts for 1 book) and $15.99 for each extra book.

How do I join Aardvark?

You can sign up for membership by downloading our mobile app or by using our website. Place your first order to kickstart your membership!

When is membership charged?

Active members are charged on the evening of the last day of the month and credits are distributed shortly after. New books drop the following morning.

How do credits work?

One credit functions as one book. If you have additional credits, you can use them to add books to your box.

What happens if I forget to order a book?

We’ve got your back! If you forget to choose or don’t like any of the selections *sad face* your credit can be used the following month as credits never expire. Please note that to opt out of the monthly fee you must skip.

How do I skip a month?

Every month, active members can choose to skip by clicking “Skip this month” under the Profile tab on our app. The deadline for choosing to skip is the 15th of the month. You can skip as many months in a row as you’d like.

When you skip a month, you don’t get billed on the next billing cycle. For example, If you skip October, you won’t be billed for November, but will be able to use your existing credit towards a November book.

To be eligible to skip you must fit all 3 criteria:

1. Be an active member for at least 1 billing cycle.

2. Not have ordered a box for that month.

3. Click “Skip this month” in-app before the 15th of the month.

Can I unskip a month?

Feeling regret? No worries, please contact support at info@aardvarkbookclub.com and we can unskip you!

How do I update my payment method?

You can update your payment method by going to Membership & Billing under your Profile and following the prompts.

Can I have more than one Aardvark account?

Absolutely! You are welcome to create as many Aardvark accounts as you would like. Please note that each account is limited to ordering 3 books per month.

How do I cancel my subscription?

We’ll be sad to see you go, but absence makes the heart grow fonder. We wouldn’t dream of you having to call us. You can cancel your membership directly on the app.

Shipping

What countries does Aardvark ship to?

We ship to the USA & Canada! Please contact support at info@aardvarkbookclub.com if you are mailing to Puerto Rico, an APO/FPO address, or PO box so we can set up your account.

Do you ship to APO/FPO, PO or Puerto Rican addresses?

We do! Please email our support team at info@aardvarkbookclub.com and they can help you set up your address.

How can I check on the shipping status of my order?

You will receive a tracking # via email as soon as your order has shipped. We aim to ship orders within a few business days of being received.

How can I confirm my order was received?

If the book(s) in your most recent order appears on the “My Shelf” tab in-app then your order has been received!

The app is not letting me enter my address - help!

Please contact support at info@aardvarkbookclub.com so we can set up your account.

How long does shipping take?

We aim to ship out orders within 1-2 business days of being received. Unless otherwise stated, all of your books will be shipped in the same box.

How do I update my shipping address?

You can update your shipping address by going to Membership & Billing under your Profile and following the prompts.

My order arrived damaged or incorrect, what do I do?

Please contact support at info@aardvarkbookclub.com with photos of any damaged books (if applicable).

Do I have to pay for shipping?

Shipping is F-R-E-E!

Books

When are new books dropped?

We drop 5-7 new books on the first of the month at 8am ET. Yes, even January 1st! We drop the 1st rain or shine, holiday or not!

Do I get to pick my books?

Yes! Every month members can select 1 book using their credit and purchase up to 2 extra books at a discount. The first book must be from the newest month’s picks but the extra books can be from any month.

What types of books do you carry?

We carry a range of genres from horror to literary fiction to romance to thriller and more! We love spotlighting debut voices and introducing our members to under-the-radar picks. We have a full-time editorial team dedicated to curating our selections.

Do you offer e-books or audiobooks?

We exclusively offer hardcover Aardvark editions with a matte dust jacket and buttery soft hardcover underneath. Check under the dust jacket and you’ll notice a foiled hardcover spine. Hardcover > ebooks any day. Our books won’t die on a trans-Atlantic flight!

Can I order a box without a book from the current month?

No, every order must include at least one book from the current month’s selections. Your add-ons (up to 2) can be from any month.

How do I remove a book from my box in-app?

You can remove a book from your box by following these steps:

1. Click the book that is on your box and view its page with the synopsis

2. Click the "View in box" button in the bottom

3. Click the top right corner of a book that you'd like to remove

Will out-of-stock books come back?

Very rarely, our team is focused on carrying upcoming picks for our members!

Do I get to keep my books?

Yes, they’re yours to read, donate, share, annotate or hoard! Loan them to friends at your own risk!

Gifting

What does a gift subscription include?

Our boxes include 3 hardcover new releases, a bookmark per book and a postcard with a monthly challenge. Each month of a gift subscription includes 3 books. For example,3 months = 9 books.

How do I give a subscription?

When you buy a gift subscription you are instantly emailed an e-gift card to print out or forward to the recipient.

How does the recipient redeem the gift subscription?

The e-gift card includes a confirmation # + instructions for redeeming the gift.

What happens to the recipient’s account when the gift ends?

The gift recipient can choose to sign up for a regular monthly membership if they’d like.

Can I gift to an existing Aardvark member?

Yes, you can give a gift subscription to an existing member and we’ll apply it to their account.

Merch

How many totes can I purchase?

Each order is limited to a maximum of 3 tote bags.

How big is the tote bag?

The tote bag is approximately 13.75 in x 15.5 in.

Will the tote bag ship with my box?

Nope, your tote bag will ship independently. You enter your mailing information on the tote checkout page. Please note: we only ship tote bags to the USA & Canada.

Do I need to be a member to buy this tote bag?

Nope! Anyone is welcome to purchase our tote bag!

Do you offer refunds or returns?

Our totes are non-refundable and we do not offer returns.

General

When did Aardvark Book Club launch?

We launched in Oct 2022 with our first-ever selections.

Why the name “Aardvark?”

1. Aardvark is the first word of the English dictionary.

2. It’s a funny looking animal. Those ears! That snout!

3. Why the hell not!

Is there a referral program?

Active members can earn a free credit for every new member they successfully refer! To earn your credit, please send us an email as soon as your friend has ordered their first box (alternatively, they can email with yours). Please note that we are unable to honour referees at the same mailing address.

Every box comes with a postcard that includes a Monthly Member Challenge. Most challenges include an opportunity to share on socials for the chance to win a free credit.

What is the Members’ Choice Award?

Every fall our members are invited to vote on their fav read of the previous 12 months of selections. The winner is announced in Dec with a special reprinting in the following Jan.

What is One Bad Night & Other Stories?

One Bad Night & Other Stories is an original Aardvark anthology we published for our 3rd anniversary in October 2025. This exclusive horror anthology featured 8 stories (never before published) by previous Aardvark authors. This title is exclusively available through Aardvark Book Club.

Please email our support team at info@aardvarkbookclub.com and we’ll try to get back to you within 1-2 business days.

Portrait of a Lady on Fire meets The Safekeep in this gripping debut that reckons with art forgery, desire, suspicion, and resistance.

In raucous 1928 Berlin, Hannah Sherman has deviated from the traditional arc of a woman’s life. An artist and a runaway, she revels in the city’s underground art scene and her newfound freedom. Working as a tailor while studying art in every spare moment, Hannah comes to know women and their bodies, first with measuring tape and silk, and later through sensuous layers of paint.

Hannah feels like she can finally call herself an artist when an intoxicating, wealthy female collector commissions an elaborate series of nude portraits. But after Hannah finishes the acclaimed Venus paintings, she discovers that her work has been tampered with and exhibited under a man’s name. When lines between artist and muse are crossed in a heady but perilous affair, Hannah transforms her work into an act of revenge, finding herself caught up in a devastating game of betrayal.

‍

Laced with queer desire and life-threatening secrets, Venus, Vanishing pulses with the hedonism and danger of 1930s Berlin as history comes to Hannah’s door, offering a heart-pounding story of Jewish survival, creativity, and resistance.

Don’t just take
our word for it

“Venus, Vanishing is so rich in nuance and complexity that I want to take a bite out of it…This novel is full of characters who talk and act like people, who make decisions real people would make. This relatability made the plot feel relevant in a way that was both unsettling and, somehow, comforting. The world has always been scary, and people have always been imperfect, but also there’s always been love and friendship and art and messy queer polycules. I’m going to be thinking about this book for a long time. ”

- Literary Hub

“Venus, Vanishing is so rich in nuance and complexity that I want to take a bite out “It’s Berlin in 1928, and Jewish artist Hannah is enjoying her newfound freedom. After Elke, a wealthy female collector, commissions an elaborate series of nude portraits, the ‘Venus’ paintings, Hannah discovers that her work has been exhibited under a man’s name and seeks revenge even as her world begins to change. Rebecca Birrell, a curator and art historian, draws on her background in the art world in her captivating debut novel. As she explains of her motivation for writing this story: During the Holocaust, ‘Art was a survival strategy. It was a means of escape and sustenance; it was an act of defiance, an affirmation of self.’”

- Town & Country

“If you loved I AM YOU by Victoria Redel (a Gays Reading book club pick last year), you'll feel right at home here. But VENUS, VANISHING hits differently right now, in a moment when both queer and Jewish visibility is under renewed threat and "just be a little less yourself" is advice many of us are hearing again, dressed up in nicer language.”

- Jason Blitman, Gays Reading Podcast

Get a taste

She only ever came to the shop with a navy wool skirt suit, tailored at an atelier in Paris. The waist needed taking in half an inch. A button re-threading. A clean and press. She couldn’t trust anyone else with it, she said. Often, the repair was so small I suspected she just wanted to be touched, admired. I never asked where she took her other clothes. Perhaps each garment required its own seamstress: There were stranger ways a woman might fill her time. I was happy to indulge the customer’s eccentricities, curious about her in the way I was about most women with money. But Mother wasn’t. The customer was nosy and overfamiliar, frankly a little odd, Mother said, smoothing a pile of folded sheets with a vigor that implied they might fight back. Mother soon found ways to occupy herself when this woman arrived, distractedly waving her in before disappearing without explanation into another room.

‍

Out of Mother’s coldness, I became this woman’s seamstress. Her clothes had an aura of quality that was impossible to ignore, like a cloud of white steam in a cold room. She was no less extraordinary. Tallness and thinness accentuated by a large  oval face and hair so fair it appeared colorless. She came from a part of Berlin that wasn’t far on the tram but as distant to me as another country. I had a precise image of her house: four stories filled with tasteful antiques, a foyer large enough for twenty guests, the upper floors still and quiet as dawn at all hours. In a low voice, she recounted trips to cities reached on sleeper trains, what might be bought at this bazaar or eaten at that tavern on the hill where locals congregated like a murmuration of birds and music could be heard late into the night. I began to look forward to her visits. When I had her in the room, I retrieved pins from my workbasket one by one, slowed my sewing hand, made subtle mistakes I would have to correct, all to lengthen her stay. When she left, insisting she wouldn’t be back for months— she would normally telephone the shop a few days later— parts of her remained in the room. A jasmine cologne so strong that I always knew the banknotes that came from her purse. Blackened matches on the floor. A clean monogrammed handkerchief, ironed flat: E.G. Mother called her Frau Grese, but when I began to take care of the suit myself, the customer insisted I call her Elke.

Book notes

  • 🙋‍♀️ Why we chose

    Venus Vanishing has prose so seductive, reading it makes you feel like you’re a Venus yourself: reclining on your velvet divan, a sheer wisp of fabric clutching at your hips, red grapes spilling into your mouth like delicate words across the page. Prose so chic you’ll feel so like you’re entangled in a multi-partnered love affair, where you can have both the handsome gallerist and the sultry cabaret dancer, your life plunging forward in step with the German avante-garde. Prose so skillful you’ll feel like a wildly successful painter, your calloused seamstress hands capable of creating something sublime, with the capacity to move an entire populace. 

    Except that moving an entire populace might not be a good thing after all…especially when your work is being displayed not as art, but as propaganda. Because the year is 1933 and a man with an unspeakable name has just been elected into power, and your patron (who also happens to be your favourite lover), might just be a sympathizer.

  • ⚠️ Content warnings

    Antisemitism, WWII setting.

  • 🙂‍↕️ The Nod by Gays Reading

    VENUS, VANISHING is Rebecca Birrell's debut novel, is ultimately a story about what it costs to hide who you are. Hannah Sherman is a Jewish artist coming of age in Weimar Berlin, attempting to establish a life as a painter, building something real for herself. When a wealthy patron offers her more (money, opportunity, a shot at the art world), Hannah is asked to sacrifice everything she has to get everything she's always wanted.

    It's historical fiction, but don't let the gallery scenes fool you. This book is about the bargains marginalized people have always been asked to make. (In this case: queer and Jewish) Birrell, an art historian by training, writes with a painter's eye for detail and a clear-eyed understanding of how erasure works.

    If you loved I AM YOU by Victoria Redel (a Gays Reading book club pick last year), you'll feel right at home here. But VENUS, VANISHING hits differently right now, in a moment when both queer and Jewish visibility is under renewed threat and "just be a little less yourself" is advice many of us are hearing again, dressed up in nicer language.

    Devastating, beautiful, and far more relevant to 2026 than any book set in 1928 has a right to be, VENUS, VANISHING earns The Nod™ by Gays Reading.
